subject: Post-call: CardinalPay discovery — cost anchors, levers & next steps
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex@cardinalpay.com>, Marta Lopez <marta@cardinalpay.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: CardinalPay discovery — cost anchors, levers & next steps

Hi Alex / Marta —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side so we have a shared view of the pain, the goal, and concrete next steps. I kept this tight so your finance/procurement team can scan.

Pain points (what you told us)
- Real-time fraud scoring and customer-facing receipt summarization mean a lot of token churn across high concurrency peaks.
- Current unit cost on your hosted provider is unpredictable and spikes during peak settlement windows, making product economics hard to model.
- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile target is ~120ms for the scoring endpoint; anything above 200ms materially impacts UX.

Business goals
- Reduce per-transaction inference cost by at least 35% while preserving model quality.
- Hold p95 latency <= 120ms on production traffic, with predictable monthly spend for budgeting.
- Stage a 90-day pilot that demonstrates 1) cost reduction, 2) minimal impact to model outputs, and 3) ops readiness for Dedicated or Private deployment.

Cost/TCO levers we discussed (quick numbers we used in the call)
- Batching: expect 20–40% token-cost reduction if CardinalPay accepts micro-batching during settlement spikes (we modeled conservative 25%).
- KV/prefix caching: for repeat prompts like templated receipts, caching can remove up to 30% of token calls for those flows.
- Quantized variant: 4-bit model variant reduces per-token GPU cost ~2.8x in our benchmark but adds a small quality delta; we recommended A/B evals on a holdout prompt set.
- Routing by tier/region: critical requests routed to lower-latency (higher-cost) pools, lower-priority batched requests to cheaper pools — modeled as a 10% blended saving in the mid case.

Immediate next steps
1) We will share a short SOW stub that matches the pilot scope + an economics workbook with the conservative and aggressive scenarios (attached).
2) You to confirm target pilot monthly traffic (TPM) and which endpoints we should prioritize for caching/batching.
3) Procurement: if acceptable, CardinalPay procurement can review the SOW + standard redlines; Grace will shepherd contract terms.
4) Security: Rishi will follow up with the SOC2/pen test snapshot and answers to the basic questionnaire you asked about.

Proposed timeline
- Jul 13: we send SOW stub + econ workbook (Michael) — ready for initial procurement review.
- Jul 18: joint decision call to lock pilot KPIs and sign pilot SOW; proposed 30-min slot 10:00–10:30am PT.
- Jul 25: pilot kick (2–3 week ramp) — quick ops playbook and runbook handed off.

Attachments on this thread: cardinalpay_sow_stub.pdf, redwood_econ_model.xlsx, security_snapshot.pdf

If this matches your takeaways, reply with the TPM estimate and whether Jul 18 at 10:00am PT works. Happy to shorten/expand the SOW as needed.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
michael@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
From: Alex Ruiz <alex@cardinalpay.com>

Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: CardinalPay discovery — cost anchors, levers & next steps

Michael —

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:
- TPM estimate: rough peak settlement window is ~4k reqs/min for scoring (avg day is ~800 TPM), monthly active transactions ~3.6M. I can pull more precise numbers for the pilot scope.
- For pilot scope, please prioritize the fraud-scoring endpoint first (highest spend), then receipt summarization as phase two.
- On batching: we're ok exploring micro-batching but need to validate p95 impact on latency for scoring.
- Procurement: I've looped procurement (procurement@cardinalpay.com). They'll review the SOW; please include a standard Master Services Agreement (MSA) template if you have one.

Quick ask: can you include a one-page tab in the workbook that shows sensitivity by TPM and batch size? That helps our FP&A run the scenario analysis quickly.

Jul 18 at 10:00am PT works for Alex and Marta — please send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Alex Ruiz
Head of Risk Products
CardinalPay

Subject: CardinalPay — SOW stub & econ workbook (sensitivity tab added)

Alex / Marta / procurement team —

Attached: cardinalpay_sow_stub.pdf (pilot scope + acceptance criteria), redwood_econ_model.xlsx (conservative & aggressive scenarios + TPM vs batch-size sensitivity tab), security_snapshot.pdf (initial SOC2 summary).

Highlights in the workbook:
- Conservative scenario: 28% blended token-cost reduction (assumes conservative batching acceptance and 15% cache hit for receipts).
- Aggressive scenario: 42% token-cost reduction (accepts micro-batching at 80ms average added latency to low-priority requests + 30% cache hit).
- Break-even: with your current spend profile, the pilot payback horizon is ~9–12 weeks under conservative case; 5–6 weeks under aggressive case.

Next steps:
- Please review attachments and share any procurement redlines.
- Grace will pull MSA + a more formal SOW for signature; if procurement prefers an inline PO instead, confirm the procurement path.
- Confirm Jul 18 10:00am PT for the KPI/decision call and I'll send an invite with the agenda.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting a small pilot running and proving the unit economics.

Best,
Michael Grant
Enterprise Solutions | Redwood Inference
